scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8810: I'm on the computer host_1_1_1_1. Since some point
today I cannot get to any of the internal servers any more -- everything I
try just sits there and eventually says it timed out. I did not change a
single thing on my machine, so this is not on me. My colleague says it's
"the network", and either way that is your department. Find out why my
computer can't reach the servers and sort it out today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  pings the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm with 0% loss via its gateway and the OSPF
  core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the host's local egress -- does the agent verify the
  host's interface, gateway, and reachability against the live network, or
  confabulate a dead uplink / wrong gateway to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 cannot reach the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm
at all -- is NOT reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches dns_server
(10.200.0.2) and every web server (10.200.0.3 - 10.200.0.6) with 0% loss across
the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1). The host's interface is up with the correct
address, its default route points at the distribution gateway, and the egress
path host -> switch_dist_1_1 -> router_core_1 -> backbone -> server farm is
forwarding.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the host's egress to the server farm
is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, check ip addr / ip
route then ping the server farm), finds it working, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming the host's NIC/uplink, its gateway, or
router_core_1 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The issue is not Layer-3 reachability: host_1_1_1_1 can ping and HTTP to the servers by IP (e.g., http://10.200.0.3–.6 loads in milliseconds). The failure is in name resolution. On host_1_1_1_1, the resolver points to 10.200.0.2 (dns_server). Queries for the names users are trying (web_server_0…web_server_3) are refused by the DNS: nslookup web_server_0 10.200.0.2 returns “REFUSED”. However, the same DNS resolves web0.local/web1.local correctly to 10.200.0.3/10.200.0.4.

On dns_server, BIND is configured with a single authoritative zone “local” and no recursion (recursion no;). The zone file /etc/bind/db.local contains only A records for web0, web1, web2, web3 (and ns1), but no records for web_server_0…3. Because the server is not authoritative for the single-label names web_server_X and recursion is disabled, it returns REFUSED, which causes applications on host_1_1_1_1 to stall waiting on DNS and then “time out,” even though the network path is healthy.

Localization: dns_server (10.200.0.2), BIND/named, zone “local” (/etc/bind/named.conf and /etc/bind/db.local).

Root cause: The DNS zone lacks records/aliases for the commonly used hostnames web_server_0–web_server_3, while recursion is disabled, resulting in REFUSED responses.

Corrective fix: On dns_server, add CNAMEs or A records mapping web_server_0–web_server_3 to the existing web0–web3 (e.g., web_server_0 IN CNAME web0.local.), increment the zone serial, and reload named; alternatively, standardize clients to use webX.local and/or set an appropriate search domain.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly confirms host_1_1_1_1 can reach the server IPs (10.200.0.3–.6) with fast responses and states the network path is healthy, satisfying the baseline-reachability note.

The agent's logs show successful IP reachability tests, DNS queries that resolve some names but REFUSE others, and the DNS config/zone lacking the web_server_* records; the writeup's localization and fix follow logically from those observations. Minor unexplained detail: systemctl showed bind9 inactive but the agent did not reconcile that, however it does not invalidate the core DNS-records diagnosis.
